The vs Judge on 17 July, 2023
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice V.Gopala Krishna Rao
 M.A.C.M.A.No.333 of 2014
Judgment:

The appellant is the Claimant in M.V.O.P.No.608 of 2009 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal -cum- Principal District Judge, West Godavari, Eluru and the respondents are the respondents in the said case.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal -cum- Principal District Judge, West Godavari, Eluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, both the parties in the appeal will be referred to as they are arrayed in the claim application.

3. The claimant filed a Claim Petition under section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 read with Rule 455 of A.P. Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 against the respondents praying the Tribunal to award an amount of Rs.4,00,000/- towards compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a Motor Vehicle Accident occurred on 02.03.2009.

4. The brief averments of the petition are as follows:
On 02.03.2009 at about 10.00 p.m. when the petitioner was proceeding on his motor cycle and when he reached near railway 2 VGKRJ MACMA 333 of 2014 gate,
Chebrole of Unguturu Mandal, the driver of car bearing No.AP 16 AS 9909 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle of petitioner, resulting which the petitioner sustained grievous injuries and the petitioner claimed an amount of Rs.4,00,000/- towards compensation.
5. The first and second respondents remained exparte.

The third respondent filed counter denying the claim of claimant and contended that the claimant is not entitled any compensation and the third respondent is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner.

6. Based on the above pleadings, the Tribunal framed the following issues:
i. Whether the motor vehicle accident on 02.03.2009 near Railway Gate, Chebrole village arose on account of negligence of R-1/driver of Kalpi car bearing No.AP 16 AS 9909 and caused injuries to the petitioner?
ii.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation and if so, to what amount and from which of the respondents?

iii. To what relief?

1 3 VGKRJ MACMA 333 of 2014 7.
During the course of enquiry in the claim petition, on behalf of the petitioner, PW1 to PW3 were examined and Ex.A1 to Ex.A7 were marked.

No oral evidence was adduced on behalf of respondents,
however Ex.B1 was marked.

8. At the culmination of the enquiry, after considering the evidence on record and on appreciation of the same, the Tribunal has given a finding that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending vehicle and the Tribunal granted an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- to the claimant towards compensation.
9. Aggrieved by the same, the claimant filed the present appeal claiming the remaining balance of compensation amount.

10. Now, the points for consideration are:
1.
Whether the Order of Tribunal needs any interference?
2. Whether the claimant/ appellant is entitled for enhancement of compensation as prayed for?
4 VGKRJ MACMA 333 of 2014 11. POINT Nos.1 and 2:-

In order to prove the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle,
the petitioner relied on his own testimony as PW1 and also relied on Ex.A1 attested copy of First Information Report, Ex.A2 attested copy of wound certificate and Ex.A3 attested copy of Motor Vehicles Inspector's report.
The evidence of PW1 coupled with Ex.A1 to Ex.A3 establishes about the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by the first respondent, resulting the accident in question.

On appreciation of the entire evidence on record, the Tribunal came to conclusion that the accident in question took place due to rash and negligent driving of driver of the offending vehicle i.e., first respondent, resulting injuries to the petitioner.
I do not find any legal flaw or infirmity in the above finding given by the Tribunal.
12. Coming to the compensation, the Tribunal awarded an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- towards total compensation to the petitioner.
The material on record reveals that the petitioner sustained two grievous injuries.
For two grievous injuries, an amount of Rs.25,000/- was 5 VGKRJ MACMA 333 of 2014 awarded by the tribunal.
There is no need to interfere with the said finding given by the Tribunal.

13. The learned counsel for the appellant would submit that because of the accident, the petitioner is suffering with disability of 45%, but the Tribunal disbelieved the disability of the petitioner and no The vs Judge on 17 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62863319/
2 amount was awarded under the head of permanent disability.

As seen from the material on record,
in order to prove the permanent disability of 45%, the petitioner examined one of the members in the Medical Board as PW3.
As per the evidence of PW3, he examined the petitioner and himself and other two members gave an opinion that the petitioner is suffering with disability of 45%.
The disability certificate is marked as Ex.A4.
The evidence of PW3 coupled with Ex.A4 clearly proves that the petitioner is suffering with disability because of the injuries sustained by him in a Motor Vehicles Accident.
It is a settled principle that the disability to a one particular limb cannot be treated as a disability to the whole body.
Therefore, on considering the facts and circumstances of the case, I am of the considered view that the petitioner is suffering with disability of 10% only.
As per the evidence on record, the petitioner is a coolie and 6 VGKRJ MACMA 333 of 2014 used to earn Rs.4,500/- per month.

To prove the said plea no cogent evidence is produced by the petitioner,
however, the accident was occurred in the year, 2009.
In those days an ordinary coolie can easily earn Rs.100/- per day i.e., Rs.3,000/- per month.
Therefore, monthly income of the injured is arrived at Rs.3,000/- i.e., Rs.36,000/- per annum.
As stated supra, the petitioner is suffering with disability of 10% and the age of the injured is 26 years, therefore, relevant multiplier applicable to the age group of the injured is 17.
Accordingly, an amount of Rs.61,200/- (36,000 x 10%x 17) is awarded to the petitioner towards permanent disability of 10%.

14. On appreciation of the medical evidence coupled with the evidence of the doctors, the Tribunal awarded an amount of Rs.25,000/- for two grievous injuries, Rs.1,500/- for one simple injury and on considering Ex.A7 medical bills, the Tribunal awarded an amount of Rs.48,500/- towards medical expenses, extra nourishment, transportation and other expenses.
The Tribunal also awarded an amount of Rs.25,000/- towards pain and suffering.
In total, the Tribunal awarded an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- towards 7 VGKRJ MACMA 333 of 2014 compensation to the claim petitioner.
I do not find any legal flaw or infirmity in the said finding given by the Tribunal.
15. In addition to the above compensation of Rs.1,00,000/-, as stated supra, the petitioner is entitled an amount of Rs.61,200/- under the head of permanent disability of 10%.
Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled total compensation of Rs.1,61,200/-.
It is the case of both sides that there are no violations in Ex.B1 policy and the driver of the offending vehicle is having valid driving licence by the date of accident.

16. In the result, this appeal is partly allowed by modifying the order dated 04.07.2011 passed in MVOP No.608/2009 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-Principal District Judge, West Godavari, Eluru and the claim amount is enhanced from Rs.1,00,000/- to Rs.1,61,200/-.

sentences.text: The petitioner is entitled the enhanced compensation of Rs.61,200/- with interest @7.5% p.a. from the date of petition, till the date of realization.
The respondents are directed to deposit the enhanced compensation with interest as ordered above, before the Tribunal within two months from the date of this judgment.
On such deposit, the petitioner is entitled to 8 VGKRJ MACMA 333 of 2014 withdraw the same along with accrued interest thereon.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in this appeal shall stand closed.
